title: A neural network shows codon arrangement influences MHC-I peptide presentation
summary: CAMAP, an artificial neural network, predicts MHC-I associated peptide presentation from mRNA sequences flanking the peptide-coding codons, and was more accurate with original than shuffled codon sequences, independently of expression and MHC-I binding affinity. In an in vitro assay, synonymous codon changes in flanking regions significantly modulated cell-surface presentation. Accuracy figures and assay effect sizes were not read.
ai_technology: CAMAP artificial neural network predicting peptide presentation from flanking codons
organization: Institute for Research in Immunology and Cancer; Université de Montréal
